q: Anecdotally all of the women I know had no issues with pregnancies 9-12 months apart so I'm always a bit surprised at how adamant redditors seem to be against smaller age gaps (although I'm aware this site it very US centric and they're more risk adverse).
cx: UK mother 11 weeks postpartum planning a quick second; professionals relaxed, Reddit strict.

q: I'm very aware of the guidance and came on to ask people's actual experiences as what I've been told by professionals and know from others is at odds with needing to wait 24 months.
cx: Same author pushing back on a commenter; wants lived experience, not the guidance restated.

q: I felt like as soon as I mentioned my anxiety over my breasts the conversation turned to learning to meditate and things like “your generation is the most anxious I have ever seen”
cx: At 23 weeks with her second, a specialist answered her worry with a generational remark.

q: it should be an exciting time for my family and now I feel like I need to tread lightly when sharing news or planning events to avoid hurting feelings.
cx: Newly pregnant with her second; a relative is struggling to conceive, joint toddler parties now awkward.

q: I am very worried about my mom specifically because she is very excited and I have a feeling that she is going to bring it up often. is there a way I can gently tell my mother not to talk about it in front of them
cx: Same author; her own mother's excitement is the risk at family gatherings.

q: I CRIED in a boardroom meeting last week. My nipples are already leaking through my bra. I can’t walk from meeting to meeting anymore and I basically have to tap out at 1:00 to sleep.
cx: First-time mother, 26 weeks, self-employed consultant, losing the ability to function at work.

q: I genuinely feel like I’m 20% of the person I was before I was pregnant and I have so much guilt for underperforming.
cx: Same author; paid on reputation, no guaranteed contract after leave.

q: I have no paid or subsidized mat leave and I don’t have a guaranteed contract upon my return to work. […] I’d be giving up 6 figures over the next 3 months if I go on mat leave early, but our financials would be “fine”
cx: Same author weighing stopping work early against income and reputation.

q: they pay me way too much for me to be doing this and I can’t bare the thought of anyone thinking I “wasn’t worth the cost”
cx: Same author on missing deadlines while pregnant.

q: I just found out they are both boys, I’m so disappointed and sad I just can’t grieve the girl I’ll never have. […] I can’t stand looking at blue clothes, cars or boys names.
cx: Pregnant with twins after a son; says this is her last pregnancy.

q: I recently found out my birth center is closing (due to government funding) […] When we started to finalize everything she tells me she’s gonna be on vacation until 8/10 my due date is 8/11. I’m freaking out again.
cx: At 30 weeks her birth centre closed; the new one is 1.5 hours away and the midwife is away near her due date.

q: I work at a call center so by about half of my shift I’m so out of breath and exhausted.
cx: Same author, 30 weeks, after a layoff left her with a supervisor she clashes with.

q: Has anyone taken one not approved by your ob or midwife but by your doctor?
cx: Same author asks about a mental-health leave signed by a GP because the new midwife can't sign until July.

q: Both practices share on-call, and both practices will discharge you if you provide negative feedback (seen in reviews).
cx: US, choosing between two OB practices; good doctor but rude staff and billing complaints vs a clean, run-of-the-mill office.

q: My OB wouldn't have to read my chart much, but a different OB would ONLY have my chart to look at and I would be a number to them, not a person.
cx: At 29 weeks, specialists want her to deliver at a bigger downtown hospital instead of with the OB she trusts.

q: I am crying almost every day trying to get dressed and feel pretty and \*glowy\* during what’s supposed to be the good part of pregnancy.

q: I think I’ll have to get over my sundress dislike and just do that because I’m spending so much unnecessary money trying to feel like myself lol.
cx: Same author after commenters suggest sundresses and thrifting.

q: it helps because I make myself feel like i am the only one by scrolling online lol
